title: Record handshake failures and inspect ClientHello
goal: Diagnose failed TLS connections in Kestrel by inspecting ClientHello bytes before HTTPS and reading the retained handshake exception after connection processing.

runtime.reason: Actual .NET 11 RC2 execution, not GA verification.
runtime.name: .NET

language.reason: Explicit sample language mode; .NET 10 comparison uses C# 14. No experimental language feature.
language.name: C#

packageAssets: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App net11.0 shared-framework assets; no added NuGet package. Older comparison uses net10.0 assets.
providers: Kestrel loopback server; no database or external resource provider.
platforms: ASP.NET Core supported server OS; actual Windows x64 TLS 1.2/1.3 execution. Fixture needs both protocol versions enabled by the OS.
renderingModes: Server HTTP endpoints; no Blazor rendering mode.
prerequisites: Use a separate directory for each complete sample below, retaining its SDK/project/package boundary. Restore required packs/packages before the sample runs. Installed Playbook guidance itself is fully offline.
Fixtures bind ephemeral loopback ports and stop their hosts. Certificates are temporary and are not added to shared trust stores.
constraints: Kestrel connection middleware, ordered around UseHttps; HTTP request middleware cannot observe a failed TLS handshake. .NET 10 callback remains valid there; .NET 11 replaces it with UseTlsClientHelloListener. Do not retain borrowed ClientHello buffers.
stabilityLimitations: Stable API intent for .NET 11, verified with RC2 under ADR 0004. Final GA reconciliation remains pending; RC2 differences are disclosed in the body.

selectionNotes: Kestrel connection middleware, ordered around UseHttps; HTTP request middleware cannot observe a failed TLS handshake. .NET 10 callback remains valid there; .NET 11 replaces it with UseTlsClientHelloListener. Do not retain borrowed ClientHello buffers.

sources.title: Official ASP.NET Core 11 capability and migration reference

evidence.scope: Actual .NET 10.0.13 loopback TLS 1.2 HTTPS success and incompatible TLS 1.3 client failure. Both ClientHellos observed through the HTTPS callback. No ITlsHandshakeFeature.Exception property exists on this target; server-side retained exception access is not claimed.

Actual .NET 11 RC2 loopback TLS 1.2 HTTPS success and incompatible TLS 1.3 failure. Ordered connection middleware observes both ClientHellos and exactly one retained AuthenticationException through ITlsHandshakeFeature after downstream completion.

humanProof.scope: All focused checks ran on the authoring machine without owner-only access. This does not settle product-wide or GA publication gates.
